title: XVII–XXIV. First table: duties toward God
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): they forbid idolatry, abuse belonging toward God's name, and violation belonging toward ye sabbath. — Ye precepts belonging toward ye former table require knowledge, love, fear, trust, and worship belonging toward God, internal and external; — XVII–XXIV. — Solemn duties belonging toward public and private worship stand as contained in ye fourth precept. — Words related toward religion stand as sanctified by ye third precept. — historical images, provided they stand as not prostituted toward worship or scandal, stand as not altogether forbidden. — Images belonging toward God toward worship stand as prohibited;
pass_b_english: XVII–XXIV. The precepts of the former table require knowledge, love, fear, trust, and worship of God, internal and external; they forbid idolatry, abuse of God's name, and violation of the sabbath.

Images of God for worship are prohibited; historical images, provided they are not prostituted to worship or scandal, are not altogether forbidden. Words related to religion are sanctified by the third precept. Solemn duties of public and private worship are contained in the fourth precept.
source_text: XVII–XXIV. Prioris tabulae praecepta exigunt Dei notitiam, amorem, timorem, fiduciam & cultum internum & externum; vetant idololatriam, abusum nominis Dei & violationem sabbati. Imagines Dei ad cultum prohibentur; historicae imagines, modo ad cultum aut scandalum non prostituantur, non prorsus vetantur. Verba ad religionem relata tertio praecepto sanctificantur. Officia solennia cultus publici & privati quarto praecepto continentur.
